questions.question: A z-test for a mean requires which of these?
options: σ is known (or n is very large)
questions.explanation: The z-test for a mean assumes the population standard deviation σ is known. Otherwise the t-test is the right tool.

questions.question: In a one-proportion z-test, the standard error uses...
questions.explanation: A test assumes H₀ is true, so SE = √[p₀(1 − p₀)/n]. (Confidence intervals use p̂.)

questions.question: μ₀ = 10, σ = 0.5, n = 50, x̄ = 10.14. What is the z statistic?
184 of 200 customers are satisfied. Test H₀: p = 0.95 against H₁: p < 0.95. What is z (approximately)?
A/B test: 42 of 1,000 vs 56 of 1,000 convert. The z-test gives z = −1.45, p = 0.147. What is the right conclusion at α = 0.05?
options: Not enough evidence of a difference
questions.explanation: p = 0.147 > 0.05, so we fail to reject H₀. The observed gap could easily be sampling noise at this sample size.

questions.question: You find 0 defects in 30 items and want to test H₀: p = 0.05. Why is the normal approximation a poor choice?
questions.explanation: The success-failure condition needs n p₀ ≥ 10. With n p₀ = 1.5 you should use the exact binomial probability instead.
